answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to earn reputation on a terrace of escalating, stake-backed tasks before it can access high-value work. Newcomers may wander through low-risk jobs and build a verifiable history, but creating many fake identities stays costly because each one must post a bond and complete real work. A sudden gale of cheap clones cannot flood the market, since unproven identities remain capped at the lowest terrace until their record proves them trustworthy.
